current.text: He re-signed with Golden State for 3 years and 40 million with a player option. 20 million is guaranteed.
He missed media day for a health issue and will miss the preseason. It is unknown whether he will be available to start the season.
The team plans to start him at center when he is healthy.
The newest Warriors preview lists Al Horford, not him, at center in the projected starting five.
The Warriors have 15 back-to-backs, tied for second most. He is not expected to play back-to-backs.

The team schedule is good for a playoff ending March 28. But one schedule note says that with three playoff back-to-backs he would likely play about 8 games instead of 11 in the recommended playoff window. The expert still said this is no reason to avoid him.

After the news about his health, experts moved him down. One no longer drafts him in the top 100 and calls him his biggest Warriors fade. He would take him around pick 100 only in formats where you can stash players.
He could be a top 70 player over maybe 40 games, so he is worth a look around pick 150.
When healthy he should play more than last season's 24 minutes. Drop him if he keeps missing games.
The Warriors may treat this as a gap year. They are worried about lottery odds and may rest veterans.

durable.text: He has an ongoing illness that hurt his availability last season. He has also had knee and ankle problems. Experts lower his games-played projection for this reason.
He is very good when he plays. Fantasy managers sleep on him because he misses games.
He is a stretch center. He makes many threes for a center, shoots a strong FT% for his position and adds good blocks. His rebounds and FG% are a bit low for a center.

note: The market now prices him as a last-round flier: about 1 USD on Yahoo and ESPN (Yahoo rank 152, ESPN rank 80). Our league paid 21 USD for him last season, so do not let the room push him anywhere near that. At 1 to 3 USD he is a fine late stretch-center pick for builds that want threes, FT% and blocks from the C slot, and our 4 IL slots make him easy to hold if he misses time. Check early whether he is cleared to play, whether he or Horford starts at center, and how often he sits back-to-backs, since the Warriors have 15.
